_comment: Dandisets that are counted as one dataset, listed by hand.
Some datasets are released as several dandisets, and papers reusing them
often cannot be told apart. A paper that reused one of them is proposed for
all of them, and the reviewer calls the one it used Reuse and the rest
Neither. Counted pair by pair, every such paper adds one confirmation and
several rejections, although the classifier was right that the paper reused
the data. What matters is that the project's data were reused, not which
dandiset the files came from.
Dandisets that name the same primary paper are grouped automatically from
the corpus (src.review.dandiset_groups.units), so they do not need listing.
This file holds the groups nothing in the metadata ties together (a
benchmark copy, a release that cites another paper of the same project) and
gives a name to groups the manuscript refers to. The two are joined: a
dandiset sharing a paper with a listed one joins the listed group.
The pairs one paper has with the dandisets of a group are counted once, as
reuse if any of them is. Reviews and the per-dandiset record in
confirmed_reuse.json are unaffected, so a paper is still credited to the
dandiset the reviewer named.
Each group gives the reason, so it can be re-examined if the dandisets are
later consolidated or come to be told apart reliably.

reason: The maze-reaching recordings of Churchland et al. 2010 and 2012:
000070 holds the full dataset, 000125 is an analysis dataset with no
data on DANDI (listed in case it is filled), and 000128,
000138, 000139 and 000140 the Neural Latents Benchmark MC_Maze task and
its Large, Medium and Small variants. Each names one or both of the
Churchland papers, and papers reusing them usually cite those papers or
the benchmark. See review_notes/mc_maze.md.
MC_RTT and NeuroTask Random Target both hold recordings from Makin et
al. 2018, which O'Doherty et al. also released on Zenodo. Papers
reusing them usually cite the paper or the Zenodo record and name
neither dandiset. See review_notes/makin_2018.md.
International Brain Laboratory releases: 000045 the behavioral data,
000149 an earlier ephys release, and 000409 the Brain Wide Map.
Papers reusing IBL data usually cite the IBL papers, which several of
these dandisets name, and reviewers attribute Brain Wide Map reuse to
000409 and call the rest Neither.
The motor cortex Patch-seq recordings of Scala et al. 2021, released
as two dandisets that both name the paper.
The Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding Neuropixels recordings of Siegle
et al. 2021, released as the Brain Observatory 1.1 and Functional
Connectivity stimulus sets. Both name the paper, they share nearly all of
their candidate papers, and papers rarely say which set they used. See
review_notes/allen_brain_observatory.md.
